summary.intent: Coordinate multiple subagents working on monokl PRs (#105 span hit ownership, #106 deterministic scaling tests, ADR 0005 PR 3) and get all open PRs conflict-free with findings resolved, after the user complained about unaddressed conflicts and findings.
summary.outcome: PR #106 and #105 were both brought to MERGEABLE with findings resolved and CI pending, and a new agent was started on ADR 0005 PR 3 stacked on #105. Nothing was merged, and the agents' results were relayed without reading the diffs.

repo: Project uses `just test`, `just lint`, `just changesets`, `just rg-compare` and `just bench` as its verification gates; PRs need a changeset.
Decisions are recorded in ADR docs (ADR 0004 for scaling, ADR 0005 for hits/blocks identified by byte spans) and in spec 05 decision log sections (e.g. §42).

Span hit ownership rules: a match at a span's end goes to the innermost block ending there only if no block holds that offset; an uncredited hit goes to the innermost blocks on its line; the sink finds each term's starts separately and merges them.
Scaling tests were converted from wall-clock ceilings to counted work (comparison counts, filter call counts, injected reader read counts), which makes them deterministic.
Dropping each file's hits early raised peak memory, so it was reverted; `regex:\b` is about +24% memory and `regex:.` about 1.6x slower versus main.
Several PRs touch the same pipeline, rank and batching code, so merge order matters (#106 before #105).

code.finding: Holds a proptest reference reimplementation that ADR 0005 PR 3 is meant to delete, along with the old text-cutting code.
Updated to state the span-ownership invariant and end rule.

workflow: Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user approval; results relayed from them should be flagged as unverified when the diff hasn't been read.
Don't start a second agent on a branch an agent is already working on, to avoid conflicting pushes.
Ask a long-running agent to push the main merge first so the PR stops conflicting before the harder fix is done.
A test that hangs when the guarded code is removed gives a poor failure signal; use a bounded step counter that panics so it fails fast (this took the lookahead test from over 2 min to 0.73 s).
Benchmark timings taken under heavy machine load (~114) are not usable evidence.

friction: The user called out unaddressed conflicts and findings after the assistant had treated #106 as a merge-order item without noticing it was conflicting and left #105 unchecked.
The #105 agent ran over an hour without pushing, and the assistant could not inspect another agent's worktree directly.
The lookahead-budget test hung for over 2 minutes instead of failing fast.
Redundant task-completion notifications repeated reports already relayed.
The stress/many benchmark was taken on a machine at load ~114, so the numbers are unreliable.
open_items: Merge #106 before #105; #97 (release) and both PRs are waiting on the user's approval, and CI is pending on them.
ADR 0005 PR 3 is in progress, stacked on #105: it must merge after #105, then retarget or merge main.
Variant V ranking-formula change is deferred to a separate PR after PR 3.
Rerun the stress/many benchmark when the machine is quiet.
The memory cost (+24% on `regex:\b`, 1.6x slower on `regex:.`) is recorded in §42 but not resolved.
The diffs of #105 and #106 have not been reviewed by the assistant.
Justified-and-left items in #106: the `nesting_tests` print, the fuzz time budget and the deadline tests.
